hero.headline: Women's Professional Baseball League unveils team names and logos ahead of August debut
hero.body:
The Women's Professional Baseball League on Wednesday unveiled the nicknames and logos of its four teams ahead of its inaugural season, with each team name inspired by pioneering women. Kelsie Whitmore, the star pitcher who was the first overall pick in the WPBL's inaugural draft, will play for the San Francisco Firebells. Mo'ne Davis, the history-making former Little League sensation, will play center field for the Los Angeles Queens, along with veteran Japanese pitcher Ayami Sato. The league also features the New York Heights and the Boston Hunters.

The WPBL's debut season begins on Aug. 1 in Springfield, Illinois. Games will be played at Robin Roberts Stadium and will run through the second half of September, including a regular season and playoffs. Whitmore told The Associated Press at a scrimmage in March that this is just every little girl's dream to play professional baseball, and now for us to actually be with each other, there's so much freedom and peace within it. The league has been years in the making and hopes to create a space for women's baseball players similar to the one the All-American Girls Professional Baseball League did 70 years ago.

Each team identity holds unique meaning. The New York Heights were inspired by Dorothy Irene Height, a pioneering civil rights and women's rights leader from New York. The San Francisco Firebells were inspired by Lillie Hitchcock Coit, known as Firebelle, who was a champion of San Francisco's volunteer firefighters. The Los Angeles Queens were created after Lizzie Murphy, a baseball pioneer known as the Queen of the Diamond. The Boston Hunters are inspired by Harriot K. Hunt, a pioneering Boston physician and women's rights activist.

The New York Heights logo includes graphic lines surrounding a baseball, mimicking the speed of a fastball and resembling the New York skyline. The San Francisco Firebells logo fuses a bell with a phoenix. The Los Angeles Queens logo is a capital Q topped with four baseball diamonds. The Boston Hunters logo is an osprey clasping a baseball bat in its talons. The team identities and names mark the beginning of the league's efforts to establish professional women's baseball.

cards.headline: Suspect identified in fatal shooting of Fort Pierce art teacher on Essex Drive
cards.body:
The St. Lucie County Sheriff's Office has identified the suspect in a shooting that killed a 66-year-old Fort Pierce man Tuesday afternoon at a home in the 2700 block of Essex Drive. Deputies responded to the residence around 3:30 p.m. after receiving reports of a person with a gunshot wound. When deputies arrived, they learned a man had shot another man with a rifle.

The victim was identified as Andre Leonard Barnes, 66, of Fort Pierce. Barnes was taken to a local hospital, where he died. The suspect has been identified as Dale A. Mincey by the St. Lucie County Sheriff's Office. Mincey remains in custody on active felony warrants out of Broward County for dealing in stolen property and false verification to a pawn broker.

Barnes was an art teacher for St. Lucie Public Schools. The district released a statement following his death. The sheriff's office said the homicide investigation remains active, and detectives continue to work with the State Attorney's Office as evidence is reviewed. Additional charges related to this investigation will be determined as the investigation progresses.

Deputies said based on information developed during the investigation, this remains an isolated incident, and there is no threat to the public. Additional information will be released as it becomes available.

cards.headline: St. Lucie County neighbors push back on 85-acre Indrio Town Center development near I-95
cards.body:
A proposed 85-acre development off Indrio Road and Russakis Road in St. Lucie County is moving closer to reality, but not without pushback from neighbors who say it will transform the area's rural character. The project, called Indrio Town Center, would bring a mix of commercial and retail space and possibly residential units to land near Interstate 95. On June 18, county planning and zoning unanimously recommended rezoning the land from agricultural to planned retail workplace. County commissioners are expected to vote on the rezoning in August.

The proposed development totals 447,250 square feet of commercial, retail and possible residential space across more than 85 acres, an area equivalent to more than 48 FIFA-standard soccer pitches. Susan Lewis has lived near the proposed site for 15 years, running a farm rescue on a property that has been in her family for decades. Lewis said the development would surround her property and worsen existing conditions. "I have dogs that have 10 acres to run around. I have horses that have 10 acres to run around. It's gone," Lewis said. "We will be surrounded. I think that there's plenty of other places for them to build." Lewis expressed concern that the development will change the rural landscape in St. Lucie County. "We moved here for a reason; this is why we do what we do," said Lewis. "We like to be in the wilderness. This is what Florida used to look like."

County Planning and Zoning Manager Kori Benton said the land is part of a planned design area called Town, Villages and Countryside, along with 14,000 other acres of land in St. Lucie County. Benton said this land was anticipated to transition from traditional legacy agricultural or citrus uses to development and will help avoid urban sprawl. "It's an overlay district that's trying to allow for tactful development and new communities that embrace the county's rural character, maintain lands for open space and agricultural activities," said Benton. "It allows for that development very strategically, that considers compatibility and how it's integrated into both the county's need for infrastructure, need for quality of life, jobs, and also connectivity to our interstate and roadway system."

Leah Heinzelmann from Cotleur and Hearing, who is representing the property owners and developer Glassman Holdings LLC, said the development will include open green space and an over 26-acre park. "The design of it incorporates a lot of open space, really keeping that native buffer along Indrio Road," Heinzelmann said. The rezoning still needs approval from county commissioners in August.

cards.headline: Three lawsuits challenge Florida property tax amendment ballot language ahead of November vote
cards.teaser: Florida's property tax amendment faces legal challenges over whether the ballot language fairly explains the measure or acts as a political sales pitch. A hearing is set for July 29.
cards.body:
Three separate legal challenges have been filed against Amendment Three by nonprofit Save Our Voters, former South Miami Mayor Philip Stoddard, and former lawmakers Jeff Brandes and Al Lawson. The plaintiffs argue the ballot language is biased, misleading and written to persuade voters rather than neutrally explain the amendment. Attorney Jamie Cole, who filed the first lawsuit, said the ballot language is very questionable and basically a political flyer. The lawsuits target several phrases in the ballot summary, including language saying the amendment would "save" homes from excessive property taxes, "protect" small businesses, "ensure" funding for core services and "ensure fairness" for Florida residents.

The amendment would expand non-school homestead property tax exemptions, eventually exempting up to $250,000 of a homestead's value by 2028. It would also limit some future assessment increases on non-homestead property and place new restrictions on how local governments use property tax dollars. State Rep. Toby Overdorf, R-Stuart, said following approval of the measure in early June that relief is coming and lawmakers are putting money back in the pockets of Floridians, provided that the state gets a 60% vote. The cases are expected to be consolidated, with a hearing currently set for July 29. If a judge agrees the ballot language is misleading, the Florida Attorney General could be tasked with rewriting the summary.

cards.headline: Indian River County responds to waste management condo fee spike in Vero Beach
cards.teaser: A Vero Beach condo owner saw his monthly waste management fees jump from $11 to $21 under a new county contract. County officials say the increase brings additional services but acknowledge the impact on residents.
cards.body:
Thomas Clark spoke with WPTV Anchor Mike Trim during a Let's Hear It event in Vero Beach about concerns regarding his monthly condo association bill. His waste management fees had jumped nearly double. WPTV brought these concerns directly to the Indian River County Department of Utility Services during a video conference meeting. The county explained that the increase stems from a new contract with Waste Management that began in October 2025. The department said the new contract raised average condo association waste management fees from $11 to $21, a roughly 93% increase. Clark told Trim he is not really happy with the increase and said he understands that if the county made a mistake, it should be on their end and suggested they maybe look at something to help residents out.

County officials say condo owners are getting additional benefits under the new contract. Himanshu Mehta of the Indian River County Solid Waste Disposal District explained that residents can now place bulk items near condo dumpsters, a service that wasn't previously available. Mehta and other county officials emphasized the importance of community involvement in public hearings, noting that this contract was approved during 2024 hearings. Mehta said if Clark or his HOA wanted to invite county staff to a meeting, they are happy to send someone to go over this process in more detail and that he and his team are available to provide that.

cards.headline: St. Lucie County offers free rip current safety training at local pools this summer
cards.teaser: St. Lucie County Parks and Recreation will host three free sessions using a new rip current simulation machine at local public pools. The training aims to teach proper escape techniques in a controlled environment.
cards.body:
St. Lucie County residents and visitors will have the chance to learn life-saving skills this summer through free rip current safety demonstrations at local public pools. The St. Lucie County Parks & Recreation Department is hosting three sessions using their new rip current simulation machine, which creates controlled currents in swimming pools to teach proper escape techniques. Jennifer Gill, St. Lucie County Parks & Recreation manager, said education is one of the most effective tools to prevent water-related emergencies. These demonstrations allow participants to experience how a rip current works in a safe, controlled environment while learning skills that could save their life or the life of someone they love.

The county has scheduled three free demonstrations this summer. On July 19, a session runs from 1 to 4 p.m. at Lakewood Park Pool with registration required and limited to 50 participants. On July 28, a session runs from 11 a.m. to 2 p.m. at Boatwright Pool as part of the Back-to-School Splash Jam event with no registration required and first-come, first-served. On August 16, a session runs from 1 to 4 p.m. at Ravenswood Pool with registration required and limited to 50 participants. According to the National Weather Service, there have been 23 rip current fatalities this year so far in the United States. The proper technique is to remain calm, swim parallel to the shoreline until escaping the current, then swim back to shore at an angle.

cards.headline: Lionel Messi leads Argentina to 3-2 comeback victory over Egypt in World Cup round of 16
cards.teaser: Lionel Messi scored his eighth goal of the tournament and led Argentina to an improbable 3-2 victory over Egypt on Tuesday despite trailing by two with only 11 minutes of regulation time to play.
cards.body:
Lionel Messi scored his record-extending 21st goal at the World Cup in the 83rd minute to level the score at 2-2. Enzo Fernandez scored the winning goal in stoppage time to complete one of the great World Cup comebacks. Cristian Romero started the rally in the 79th minute. The defending champions will next face either Switzerland or Colombia in the quarterfinals on Saturday in Kansas City, Missouri. Messi, who was in tears after the final whistle, scored his eighth goal of the tournament despite Argentina trailing by two with only 11 minutes of regulation time to play. Argentina is bidding to become the first team to win back-to-back titles since Brazil did so in 1958 and 1962.

Argentina had trailed 2-0 on goals from Yasser Ibrahim and Mostafa Zico. Egypt took a surprising lead in the 15th minute when Ibrahim got ahead of Lisandro Martinez to meet Marwan Attia's cross and head the ball into the bottom corner. Messi missed a chance in the first half when his penalty kick was saved by Egypt goalkeeper Mostafa Shobeir after referee François Letexier pointed to the penalty spot when Haissem Hassan tripped Nicolas Tagliafico in the box. Messi later hit the post when the score was 1-0. Egypt thought it had doubled its lead in the second half when Zico finished off a sweeping attack, but the wild celebrations were cut short when a foul earlier in the move was confirmed on video review and the goal was disallowed. That second goal for Egypt did come in the 67th from a similar break, and this time Zico's effort counted.

cards.headline: United States eliminated from World Cup after 4-1 loss to Belgium
cards.teaser: The United States hopes for a deep World Cup run at home ended when Charles De Ketelaere scored twice and assisted on another goal, helping Belgium defeat the Americans 4-1 on Monday night in the round of 16.
cards.body:
Charles De Ketelaere scored twice and assisted on another goal to lead Belgium to a 4-1 victory over the United States on Monday night, earning the Red Devils a quarterfinal berth and eliminating the Americans from the World Cup. Second-half substitute Romelu Lukaku added Belgium's final goal in the third minute of stoppage time. Seeking its first World Cup title, Belgium knocked the U.S. out in the round of 16 for the second time in 12 years and extended its unbeaten streak to 18 games. The Red Devils play 2010 champion Spain on Friday at Inglewood, California, for a semifinal berth against France or Morocco.

De Ketelaere put Belgium ahead in the eighth minute, the first time in this year's World Cup the U.S. conceded first. Malik Tillman tied the score 1-1 midway through the first half with his second free kick goal of the tournament, but the Americans conceded just 61 seconds after the ensuing kickoff when De Ketelaere scored his second goal in the 33rd minute. Coach Mauricio Pochettino showed his frustration by kicking a rack in front of the bench, sending four water bottles flying. Hans Vanaken made it 3-1 in the 57th minute after goalkeeper Matt Freese lost control of the ball in front of his net. American star Christian Pulisic could only watch from the bench after injuring his right foot when he hit a boot of Belgium captain Youri Tielemans on a 52nd-minute shot attempt.

cards.headline: Monday's US-Belgium World Cup match draws biggest soccer audience in US history
cards.teaser: Monday's United States-Belgium World Cup match drew more than 30 million viewers, making it the most-watched soccer telecast in U.S. history, Fox Sports reported.
cards.body:
According to Fox Sports, Monday's United States-Belgium World Cup match drew more than 30 million viewers, making it the most-watched soccer telecast in U.S. history. Viewership peaked at 36 million early in the second half of Monday's match. The United States lost 4-1 to Belgium. Telemundo said its Spanish-language broadcast reached 12 million viewers, which NBCUniversal said is a record for a U.S. men's national team broadcast. Interest in Monday's match intensified after FIFA announced that Folarin Balogun would be eligible to play against Belgium despite receiving a red card last week against Bosnia and Herzegovina.

The United States' match against Bosnia and Herzegovina also set records. Fox said about 26.4 million viewers tuned in, setting what was then the record for an English-language soccer broadcast in the United States. Telemundo said it drew 9.8 million viewers, the largest Spanish-language audience for a U.S. men's national team match. Fox said its World Cup broadcasts have generated significant interest beyond U.S. matches. The network said last week's Portugal-Croatia match drew more than 11 million viewers, making it the most-watched World Cup match on Fox that did not involve the United States or a final. Fox also said its Mexico-Ecuador broadcast last week drew more than 10 million viewers. Telemundo said its Mexico-England broadcast delivered 23.1 million viewers.

cards.headline: IOC ends neutral status vetting for Russian athletes ahead of 2028 LA Olympics
cards.teaser: The International Olympic Committee advised Olympic sports bodies on Tuesday to end a three-year program vetting Russians for neutral status ahead of qualifying events for the 2028 Los Angeles Olympics.
cards.body:
The International Olympic Committee advised Olympic sports bodies on Tuesday to end a three-year program vetting Russians for neutral status ahead of qualifying events for the 2028 Los Angeles Olympics. The move was expected since the IOC advised two months ago that athletes from Belarus, Russia's military ally in the full military invasion of Ukraine, should be allowed again to compete with their full national identity. The IOC eased entry requirements to its own events for Russian athletes and teams while provisionally lifting its suspension since October 2023 of the Russian Olympic Committee. The terms of that suspension, imposed when the Russian Olympic body incorporated regional sports councils from occupied regions of Ukraine, no longer applied, the IOC said.

Just 32 athletes from Russia and Belarus competed at the 2024 Paris Olympics as approved neutrals and combined to win five medals. The Russian team had more than 300 athletes at the 2021 Tokyo Olympics and won 71 medals. The IOC did not yet approve letting Russian athletes and teams compete with their flag and anthem. That decision will come at an appropriate time, it said. The IOC said to address the lack of confidence in the global sporting community relating to the return of Russian athletes to international competition, those athletes must give multiple doping controls and be part of a recognized testing program. The IOC said it will continue to not organize IOC events in Russia or invite Russian government or state officials to its events.

hero.headline: 18th Annual Treasure Coast Seafood Festival Returns to Vero Beach in November
hero.body:
The 18th Annual Treasure Coast Seafood Festival will return to Vero Beach this November, according to Under The Sun Promotions, Inc. The annual event brings seafood vendors, entertainment, and family activities to Indian River County each year.

The festival has become a tradition in Vero Beach, drawing visitors from across the Treasure Coast and beyond. Under The Sun Promotions organizes the multi-day event that showcases local seafood and regional cuisine.

The November date marks the festival's return for its 18th consecutive year in Vero Beach. Organizers said the event will feature seafood from vendors throughout Florida and the Southeast.

Festival planners will release additional details about the specific dates, location, vendors, and entertainment lineup in the coming months. The event typically takes place at a waterfront location in Vero Beach during November.

hero.headline: Colorado State University reduces 2026 Atlantic hurricane season forecast
hero.teaser: Colorado State University lowered its 2026 Atlantic hurricane season forecast due to a strong El Niño pattern.
hero.body:
Colorado State University has reduced its forecast for the 2025 Atlantic hurricane season, prompting adjustments in expectations across Florida and other coastal states. The reduction is attributed to what forecasters are calling a "beyond super" El Niño pattern affecting atmospheric conditions in the Atlantic basin. The university's Tropical Meteorology Project, which issues widely watched seasonal forecasts, announced the downgrade, with the season now projected to be "well below normal."

The revised forecast comes as the Atlantic basin experiences exceptionally strong El Niño conditions that meteorologists say will significantly suppress hurricane activity. El Niño conditions typically reduce Atlantic hurricane formation by increasing wind shear, which disrupts storm development. The powerful El Niño this year has prompted the research team to slash expectations for named storms, hurricanes, and major hurricanes compared to earlier predictions. Hurricane season runs from June 1 through November 30.

Despite the lower overall forecast, meteorologists including FOX Weather's Bryan Norcross note that coastal residents should remain vigilant for storms developing close to the coast. Even in suppressed seasons, storms that form near land can rapidly intensify and pose threats to coastal communities. The Gulf Coast and Atlantic coastal regions will need to monitor conditions throughout the season, as localized threats can still emerge regardless of broader atmospheric patterns that limit overall activity.

The updated forecast affects emergency planning and insurance considerations across Florida and other coastal states. Local emergency management agencies and insurance companies use these seasonal predictions to allocate resources and adjust risk assessments. While a below-normal season reduces the statistical likelihood of major impacts, forecasters emphasize that it only takes one storm making landfall to create a devastating season for affected communities. Coastal residents are encouraged to maintain their hurricane preparedness plans and supplies regardless of seasonal predictions, as the reduced forecast does not eliminate the threat entirely.

cards.headline: Former Florida gubernatorial candidate Andrew Gillum arrested on drug possession charges in Alabama
cards.teaser: Andrew Gillum, who narrowly lost the 2018 Florida governor's race to Ron DeSantis, was arrested on marijuana and methamphetamine possession charges after a traffic stop in Daphne, Alabama.
cards.body:
Former Florida gubernatorial candidate Andrew Gillum was arrested on drug possession charges in Alabama after police say they pulled him over for erratic driving and found marijuana and meth in his vehicle. Gillum, 46, was arrested on July 2 in Daphne, about 11 miles east of Mobile on Alabama's Gulf Coast. He is charged with marijuana possession and unlawful possession of a controlled substance, the Daphne Police Department said. Jail records show he was released on July 3. The Daphne Police Department said officers stopped Gillum's vehicle around 10:45 p.m. and initiated a probable cause search after one of them noticed a glass pipe on the center console. They found several rolled marijuana cigarettes and three packages of a substance that tested positive for methamphetamine.

Gillum served as mayor of Florida's capital from 2014 to 2018 and came within less than a percentage point of being elected the state's first Black governor, losing to Republican Ron DeSantis by fewer than 34,000 votes. In 2022, Gillum was indicted on federal conspiracy and wire fraud charges for allegedly funneling tens of thousands of dollars in campaign donations through third parties back to himself for personal use. A 2023 trial ended in a hung jury on those charges and an acquittal on charges that Gillum lied to undercover FBI agents posing as developers who paid for a 2016 trip he took with his brother to New York, including hotel rooms, meals, a boat tour and a ticket to the hit Broadway show "Hamilton." Gillum is a co-host of the politically themed Native Land Pod, which won the NAACP Image Award for Outstanding News and Information Podcast in 2025.

cards.headline: Bryan Norcross warns Florida to watch for close-to-coast storm development despite reduced hurricane forecast
cards.teaser: Meteorologist Bryan Norcross says Florida should remain vigilant for storms developing near the coast even as the hurricane season forecast gets reduced.
cards.body:
Meteorologist Bryan Norcross cautioned that Florida should watch for storms developing close to the coast as the hurricane season forecast gets reduced. Despite lower overall seasonal projections, Norcross emphasized that storms forming near the coastline remain a threat that requires attention from residents and emergency managers across the state.

The warning comes as Colorado State University reduced its 2026 Atlantic hurricane season forecast due to strong El Niño conditions. Norcross noted that while El Niño patterns typically suppress Atlantic hurricane activity overall, they do not eliminate the risk of storms that form quickly near shore. These close-to-coast systems can develop rapidly and give residents less time to prepare, making them particularly dangerous even in below-normal seasons. Florida's geography, with extensive coastline on both the Atlantic Ocean and Gulf of Mexico, makes the state vulnerable to such systems regardless of broader seasonal trends.

cards.headline: FixMold completes 7,000 mold assessments in South Florida during 2025
cards.teaser: FixMold reached 7,000 completed mold assessments in South Florida during 2025, establishing itself as a major provider in the region.
cards.body:
FixMold completed 7,000 mold assessments in South Florida during 2025, reaching a milestone that positions the company as a leading provider of mold assessment services in the region. The company announced the achievement as it continues operations in 2026, serving residential and commercial clients across South Florida's counties.

The high volume of mold assessments reflects ongoing concerns about mold growth in South Florida's humid climate. Properties in the region face elevated risk of mold contamination due to moisture, flooding, and weather events. FixMold's assessment services help property owners identify mold problems and determine remediation needs. The company's growth in South Florida comes as property owners and managers seek professional evaluation of indoor air quality and structural conditions related to mold presence.

hero.headline: 85-acre Indrio Town Center development near I-95 faces pushback from St. Lucie County neighbors
hero.teaser: A proposed 85-acre mixed-use development off Indrio Road and Russakis Road in St. Lucie County is moving toward reality after county planning and zoning unanimously recommended rezoning the agricultural land. County commissioners are expected to vote on the rezoning in August.
hero.body:
A proposed 85-acre development near Indrio Road and Russakis Road in St. Lucie County is advancing despite concerns from neighbors about losing the area's rural character. The project, called Indrio Town Center, would bring 447,250 square feet of commercial, retail and possible residential space to land near Interstate 95. On June 18, county planning and zoning unanimously recommended rezoning the land from agricultural to planned retail workplace. County commissioners are expected to vote on the rezoning in August.

Susan Lewis, who has lived near the proposed site for 15 years running a farm rescue on family property that has been in her family for decades, said the development would surround her property and worsen existing conditions. "We will be surrounded," Lewis said. "I think that there's plenty of other places for them to build." She expressed concern about losing space for her animals and the transformation of the rural landscape. "We moved here for a reason; this is why we do what we do," Lewis said. "We like to be in the wilderness. This is what Florida used to look like."

County Planning and Zoning Manager Kori Benton said the land is part of a planned design area called Town, Villages and Countryside, along with 14,000 other acres of land in St. Lucie County. Benton said this land was anticipated to transition from traditional legacy agricultural or citrus uses to development and will help avoid urban sprawl. "It's an overlay district that's trying to allow for tactful development and new communities that embrace the county's rural character, maintain lands for open space and agricultural activities," Benton said. "It allows for that development very strategically, that considers compatibility and how it's integrated into both the county's need for infrastructure, need for quality of life, jobs, and also connectivity to our interstate and roadway system."

Leah Heinzelmann from Cotleur and Hearing, representing the property owners and developer Glassman Holdings LLC, said the development will include open green space and an over 26-acre park. "The design of it incorporates a lot of open space, really keeping that native buffer along Indrio Road," Heinzelmann said. The proposed development area is equivalent to more than 48 FIFA-standard soccer pitches. The rezoning still needs approval from county commissioners in August.

cards.headline: Suspect identified in shooting death of Fort Pierce art teacher Andre Leonard Barnes
cards.body:
The St. Lucie County Sheriff's Office has identified the suspect in a fatal shooting that killed a 66-year-old Fort Pierce man Tuesday afternoon. Andre Leonard Barnes died at a local hospital after being shot with a rifle at a residence in the 2700 block of Essex Drive. Deputies responded to the home at around 3:30 p.m. Tuesday after receiving reports of a person with a gunshot wound. When deputies arrived, they learned a man had shot Barnes with a rifle.

The suspect has been identified as Dale Mincey. Mincey remains in custody on active felony warrants out of Broward County for dealing in stolen property and false verification to a pawn broker. Barnes was an art teacher for St. Lucie County schools, and the district released a statement following his death. The homicide investigation remains active, and detectives continue to work with the State Attorney's Office as evidence is reviewed. Additional charges related to this investigation will be determined as the investigation progresses. Deputies said based on the information developed during the investigation, this remains an isolated incident, and there is no threat to the public.

cards.headline: St. Lucie County offers free rip current safety training at local pools this summer
cards.teaser: St. Lucie County Parks & Recreation Department is hosting three free rip current safety demonstrations using a new simulation machine that creates controlled currents in swimming pools to teach proper escape techniques.
cards.body:
St. Lucie County residents and visitors can attend free rip current safety demonstrations this summer at local public pools. The St. Lucie County Parks & Recreation Department is hosting three sessions using their new rip current simulation machine, which creates controlled currents in swimming pools to teach proper escape techniques. On July 19, a session runs from 1 to 4 p.m. at Lakewood Park Pool, requiring registration and limited to 50 participants. On July 28, a demonstration runs from 11 a.m. to 2 p.m. at Boatwright Pool as part of the Back-to-School Splash Jam event, with no registration required on a first-come, first-served basis. On August 16, another session runs from 1 to 4 p.m. at Ravenswood Pool, requiring registration and limited to 50 participants.

Jennifer Gill, St. Lucie County Parks & Recreation manager, said education is one of the most effective tools to prevent water-related emergencies. The demonstrations allow participants to experience how a rip current works in a safe, controlled environment while learning skills that could save their life or the life of someone they love. According to the National Weather Service, there have been 23 rip current fatalities this year so far in the United States. The proper technique when caught in a rip current is to remain calm, swim parallel to the shoreline until escaping the current, then swim back to shore at an angle.

cards.headline: Port St. Lucie real estate expert shares relocation tips with HelloNation
cards.teaser: Port St. Lucie real estate expert Karriemah Lashley is sharing relocation tips for people moving to the area through HelloNation.
cards.body:
Lashley, a local real estate professional, provided guidance for those considering relocating to Port St. Lucie. The tips were shared through HelloNation, a platform connecting residents with local experts.

The information aims to help prospective residents understand the Port St. Lucie area and make informed decisions about moving to the city. Port St. Lucie continues to attract new residents to the Treasure Coast region.
